calibration.source: One shared parent-policy TRAIN sample, complete episodes only; 80/20 source-group fit/monitor; fixed fit steps, no selection.
calibration.target: Unshaped Monte Carlo combat return; identical targets and minibatch stream per paired seed; separate frozen representation vectors.

compatibility.semantics: Same snapshots, source campaigns, splits and public starts. Previously used validation is development data. No new heldout claim.

initialization: Common selected250k rich-combat graph actor. Shared non-name actor tensors copied exactly. Existing name rows remapped by string. All new rows equal parent unknown row to isolate learning new identities from random input disruption. Identical fresh critic weights per seed before per-arm TRAIN calibration. Fresh PPO optimizer, paired RNG/cursors; native counters start at0. Full descriptions can immediately change predictions; measured before training.
interpretation:
This pilot does not show a convincing combat improvement from either representation change. Mean greedy validation is 50.0% for legacy, 51.2% for complete vocabulary, and 48.8% with descriptions. Mean sampled validation is 49.4%, 46.4%, and 47.0%, respectively. The selected 250k parent remains ahead at 61.9% greedy and 54.8% sampled.

Complete vocabulary adds one greedy win in seed a and ties seed b; sampled differences versus control are +1 and -6 games. Descriptions lose one greedy win per seed versus the equal-capacity vocabulary arm; their sampled differences are -3 and +4 games. These small, inconsistent changes do not justify promotion or a larger continuation budget.

Descriptions leave Vantom 2.85 and 0.63 HP lower on shared losses versus matched controls, but completed player HP on shared wins changes -0.83 and +0.70 HP. Vocabulary-only loss HP changes -4.05 and +1.88 HP. These conditional diagnostics do not establish an overall improvement. All endpoints regress from their own initial greedy scores.

The richer inputs are inexpensive here: PPO averages 4m22s for legacy, 4m25s for complete vocabulary, and 4m27s for descriptions. Different learned trajectories contribute to these timings; this is not an isolated encoder microbenchmark.

Keep the selected 250k specialist as the reference. Coverage fixes remain useful for representing public information, but they are not evidence of better decisions. This experiment tests 50k adaptation of an inherited actor with matched fresh critics and optimizers. It does not settle whether using these features from initial training helps. A matched comparison from the same earlier training stage is the next representation-specific question; broader training-state coverage is a separate data experiment. The 57 reserved test openings remain untouched.
limitations: Two fine-tuning schedules share one historically validation-selected parent; not independent pretrained learners.
Repeated development-validation use; no new test confirmation and no population-wide claim.
Complete vocabulary changes identity/structural token coverage and model capacity; metadata versus vocabulary holds capacity fixed.
Static descriptions are partial mechanical features, not an exact simulator or textual reasoning model.
This 50k adaptation study does not test from-scratch learning, longer budgets, other bosses or full-run performance.

protocol.primary: Fixed50k validation greedy wins per paired seed versus control. Full descriptions versus complete-vocabulary-only isolates added fields at equal parameter count; zero-shot diagnostic separates transfer disruption.
protocol.secondary: Sampled wins, common-loss boss HP, common-win completed player HP, unconditional boss HP, training win rate, speed.
protocol.selection: No early stopping, no automatic promotion; reserved test remains closed.
protocol.uncertainty: Two forks from one selected parent and repeatedly used42-case development validation; not independently pretrained seeds or heldout confirmation.

question: Do complete public vocabulary and static potion/relic descriptions improve Vantom combat fine-tuning?

results.hp_definition: Winning HP uses canonical completed CombatSummary after post-combat hooks, matching the reward. Raw evaluation player_hp is before those hooks and is not used for the headline metric. Boss HP comes from the retained stable enemy slot.
results.interpretation: Exploratory two-seed catalog-representation pilot from one inherited actor after matched TRAIN-only value calibration. New names start from the unknown embedding. Description fields can change the initial behavior; zero-shot performance is measured. Final 50k is primary; 0/25k are diagnostics. The parent was previously selected on this reused validation and every arm inherits it. No independent test confirmation. Conditional HP means can change when win/loss populations change; common-outcome deltas are paired.

variants.control: Legacy observed vocabulary; unchanged public inputs
variants.descriptions: All identities plus frozen potion/relic descriptions; same new embedding initialization
variants.identities: Complete catalog vocabulary (entities and structural/value tokens), empty metadata fields; new embeddings initially equal legacy unknown

findings: No preparation ownership/revalidation blocker; all20 inherited reservations validated.
No blocking training/evaluation issue;300k PPO+4096 TRAIN calibration,1992 evaluations.
